title: Long LMT — Iran Operations Driving JASSM/GMLRS/PAC-3 Reorder Cycle
entry: Initiate $510-522 on June 2 or June 3, confirming Iran talks remain suspended (no diplomatic breakthrough headline). Scale: 60% at open if LMT is trading above $510; add 40% on any intraday pullback to $510-514. Do not initiate if Brent closes below $91 for two consecutive sessions — that would signal Iran de-escalation removing the primary catalyst.
stop_loss: $498 daily close (~3.6% below entry midpoint $516) — implies a formal Iran ceasefire announcement OR Brent collapse below $88 signaling rapid Hormuz reopening, eliminating the precision-weapons reorder cycle thesis
targets: $540 — initial DoD emergency supplemental authorization reported: media confirmation of JASSM-ER and GMLRS reorder requests to replenish May 27-28 strike stockpiles; regional allied F-35 system orders initiated, +4.5%
$562 — Saudi Arabia and UAE additional Patriot PAC-3 and THAAD orders formalized in DoD FY2027 budget supplemental request; LMT backlog upgraded in next quarterly update, +8.8%

$590 — full Iran conflict duration premium expansion: operations extend beyond 30 days, triggering DoD multi-year procurement authorization for LMT's precision-strike portfolio; analyst consensus target upgrades, +14.2%
catalyst: US military strikes on Iranian facilities (May 27-28) and confirmed IRGC warning shots at four vessels near the Strait of Hormuz (May 29) represent the transition from deterrence posturing to active kinetics — a categorically different demand profile for Lockheed Martin's precision weapons portfolio. The relevant systems are JASSM-ER (the primary stand-off strike weapon used in the facility strikes), GMLRS (GPS-guided rockets for HIMARS systems deployed to regional bases), and the PAC-3 MSE interceptor (the active air-defense layer protecting US and allied assets from IRGC retaliation). Each kinetic engagement depletes inventory that requires near-term replenishment under DoD rapid-replenishment authorities.
thesis:
Lockheed Martin's FY2026 revenue mix is approximately 40% Missiles and Fire Control — the segment most directly tied to replenishment demand from active operations. When the US military conducts precision strikes against Iranian facilities using JASSM-ER, the depleted inventory is governed by DoD's Section 506 drawdown authority, which triggers Congressional notification and replacement procurement authorization within 30-45 days of drawdown. LMT's supply chain for JASSM-ER carries 12-18 month production lead times, meaning emergency supplemental authorizations beginning in June will appear as backlog additions in the August-September period — likely coinciding with LMT's Q2 2026 earnings call timing and providing a visible forward revenue signal.

The Iran operations also create indirect demand through allied military responses. Saudi Arabia and the UAE have both had active Patriot PAC-3 and F-35 procurement discussions ongoing since 2024; the confirmed May 2026 IRGC escalation against Hormuz shipping validates their threat assessments and will accelerate formal Letters of Request. These allied sales, once converted to Letters of Acceptance, add to LMT's backlog with 90-120 day recognition timelines. LMT's Missiles and Fire Control segment has a current program of record backlog of approximately $14B and operates at sustained production rates — marginal JASSM and PAC-3 additions from emergency replenishment are high-margin incremental revenue at already-absorbed overhead.

This setup is distinct from the existing NOC long (which centers on B-21 Raider strategic bomber and ISR platforms — longer-lead, lower-volume systems) and the closed ITA ETF long (which captured the initial sector re-rating). LMT represents the precision-kinetics layer of the Iran operation: every strike, every intercept, and every allied deterrence reinforcement flows through Missiles and Fire Control. The thesis has a concrete near-term trigger — DoD emergency replenishment authorization, typically reported by Defense News or Reuters within 30 days of confirmed drawdown operations — making the catalyst timeline visible rather than speculative.

Iran talks remain explicitly suspended as of the June 2 Tasnim agency report. Brent at $94.58 is $2.42 from the $97 mandatory XLE short-cover trigger. Every additional day without a diplomatic off-ramp extends the reorder cycle window. The $498 stop captures a scenario where rapid de-escalation forces a sector reversal before the DoD authorization is formalized.
bull_case: Iran operations extend through June 17 FOMC with no ceasefire signal. DoD emergency supplemental request for JASSM-ER and GMLRS replenishment is transmitted to Congress and reported by Defense News. Saudi Arabia formal Letter of Request for additional F-35 units surfaces from DoD FY2027 supplemental request. LMT gaps toward $540+ on confirmation. Stretch: Congressional authorization for an Iran conflict supplemental adds $8-12B to LMT's 5-year addressable contract pipeline; Q2 2026 earnings guidance is raised above consensus.
bear_case: Iran and the US reach a diplomatic back-channel agreement (Pakistan-mediated, as referenced in the June 2 morning briefing) before June 8; Brent falls to $87-88 on Hormuz reopening expectation. LMT reverses 5-8% intraday on ceasefire headline, triggering the $498 stop before the DoD replenishment authorization cycle is formalized. The kinetics phase proves to be a 72-96 hour event, and the reorder cycle is deferred to the regular FY2027 budget process rather than an emergency supplemental.
invalidation: Formal US-Iran ceasefire or Hormuz reopening announcement, OR Brent daily close below $88, OR ITA ETF declines more than 3% in a single session (signals broad defense de-rating rather than LMT-specific re-rating)

outcome.outcome_label: Target 1 hit at $540 — LMT reached $546.94; Brent invalidation triggered simultaneously
outcome.note: LMT reached $546.94 on June 12, clearing Target 1 at $540 (+6.0% from $516 entry midpoint). Simultaneously, the Iran-US 60-day ceasefire framework (Trump announcement June 11) sent Brent toward $86.91 — below the explicit $88 Brent invalidation condition. Both T1 profit and invalidation fired on the same day. T1 taken. The precision-weapons reorder cycle thesis remains valid long-term but the ceasefire removes the near-term urgency premium.
